You know what... scratch that... just play Star Control 2.

Mass Effect ripped off half their game from Star Control 2. It's got an impressively deep story and gameplay that makes you think the game world is both real, and insanely big.

A close second is System Shock 2. Get the texture packs but NOT the 3-d model packs. The new 3-d models look nothing like the originals and don't fit/bring you out of the game. I have no idea how people can love Bioshock, or compare it to System Shock 2. Bioshock is an action shooter, System Shock 2 is a slow moving action-RPG with inventory management.

Star Control is the one on the list I hadn't heard of before, but I'll definitely take a look. Much of your list is single-player games with engaging story lines, which I always enjoy even though I don't make enough time for them lately.
Go with 2. It's waaaay better. In fact, you can get a remastered version for the low low price of $0. You won't regret this. It's a damn epic space adventure with fun real-time arcade style combat.
Heroes of Might and Magic 2 or 3. While 3 has better graphics and more types of castles / units, I just prefer the feel of 2 (possibly because I played it so much as a kid).
You can't beat the nostalgia factor :) thanks for the recommendation!
Tearaway, because it's an amazing game that so few experienced. I think it's the best game of the last 5 years.
The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth. It's one of the best indie games I've played since FTL.
I Wanna Be The Guy, and you cannot play any other game until you beat it.

Cave Story. A simple and charming game made by a guy in his spare time. It's what indie games should strive for. Not fancy graphics or a convoluted story, but a game that's fun to play.

It also helps that it's hard as shit when you play on the hardest difficulty and try to get the true ending. GODDAMN IT WHY!?
Dwarf Fortress. It has one hell of a learning curve, but the possibilites and FUN are endless.

Hotline Miami. Music is incredible, combat is solid and brutal and the sense of mystery all the way through is great. It's like a detective story where you aren't the detective and are just being pushed around a a pawn. The sequel doesn't have as good gameplay (a lot of maps feel very unfair as enemies can see you while you can't see them), but has an interesting story and a nice variety of combat styles. Oh, Teleglitch is an awesome top down horror rogue like that I love too.
